books.section: Topic 1.4 Columbian Exchange, Spanish Exploration, and Conquest
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: The Americas gained new foods while Europe lost people to disease and war.
options.misconception: The direction is backwards: disease devastated the Americas, while Europe gained the foods.

options.text: Both directions carried the same goods in equal amounts to people on both sides.
options.misconception: The flows were not equal; the dying went one way and the gains went mostly the other.

options.text: Neither direction changed daily life for ordinary people on either side of the ocean.
options.misconception: The Exchange changed daily life everywhere: new foods, new animals, new diseases, new labor systems.

options.text: Europe gained foods that fed growth; the Americas lost people to disease and labor.

rationales.general:
1. Make two lists. Europe gained maize, potatoes, and tomatoes that fed more people.
2. Make the other list. The Americas lost people to epidemics and to forced labor.
3. Compare the two lists. The gains and the losses did not fall on the same side.
4. Rule out the rest. The flows were not equal, the direction in C is backwards, and daily life changed everywhere.
Remember: to compare two directions, list gains and losses for each side separately.
rationales.D: Europe gained foods that fed growth; the Americas lost people to disease and forced labor. The two directions were not alike.
rationales.A: The direction is backwards. Disease devastated the Americas, while Europe gained the foods.
rationales.B: The flows were not equal. The dying went one way and the gains went mostly the other.
rationales.C: The Exchange changed daily life everywhere: new foods, new animals, new diseases, new labor systems.

stem: Which comparison best captures the difference between the two directions of the Columbian Exchange?

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, stating the argument the questions evaluate.
stimulus.text: A historian argues that the Columbian Exchange was an exchange of goods between the Eastern and Western Hemispheres that spread prosperity to people on both sides of the Atlantic.
